children: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is "managing an unusually partisan Fed," Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said on Wednesday.

Part of that he blamed on Jerome Powell not resigning after his term as Fed chair ended. Also, Michael Barr, who had been vice chair for supervision, has remained on the board to serve out his term as a Fed governor.

Traditionally, Fed chairs and vice chairs have resigned when their terms in those roles expire. Powell has said he's staying on the board until he's satisfied that all investigations against him and Lisa Cook have been resolved.

Hassett implied that the Fed was adjusting its benchmark interest rate for politically motivated reasons, noting that the central bank hiked rates right after President Trump's his first term in office started and before the midterms then cut before the 2024 election.

target range by a quarter of a percentage point to 3.75%. "I'm worried about why they did that," he said in a moderated conversation at a Georgetown University event.

If you take the last three months of core inflation and annualize it, you get ~2%, Hassett said. In that case, rates don't need to be raised, he added. "If the core is 2, then why are you hiking?" he posited.
"A lot of people who weren't appointed by President Trump are giving a lot of speeches in the last couple of days saying we need more hikes," he said.
"I think there's still some work to do to restore Fed independence, and I know that's something that's high on the priority list for Kevin," Hassett stated.
